# Forms

`<location-picker>` is a form-associated custom element (built on `ElementInternals`). Inside a `<form>` it behaves like a native input: it submits a value, takes part in validation, resets with the form and restores its state on back/forward navigation.

## What gets submitted

Pick the names you want. The value is always latitude first, dot decimal, no spaces.

| Configuration                               | Entries when set                      | Entries when unset           |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `name="loc"`                                | `loc=48.85837,2.294481`               | `loc=`                       |
| `lat-name="lat" lng-name="lng"`             | `lat=48.85837`, `lng=2.294481`        | `lat=`, `lng=`               |
| `name` + `lat-name` + `lng-name`            | all three                             | all three empty              |
| `+ address-name="addr"`                     | `addr=<address>` (`""` while unknown) | `addr=`                      |
| none of the above                           | none                                  | none; validation still works |
| `disabled`, or inside `<fieldset disabled>` | none                                  | none                         |

`address-name` needs `search` or `reverse-geocode`. The address may arrive a moment after the coordinates (reverse geocoding is debounced by 400 ms).

```html
<form method="post" action="/stores">
  <label for="loc">Store location</label>
  <location-picker
    id="loc"
    name="location"
    lat-name="lat"
    lng-name="lng"
    required
    search
    style="height: 360px"
  ></location-picker>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

## Bound inputs

When the page already has inputs, let the picker fill them instead of adding its own entries. Pass an id (tried first) or a CSS selector:

| Attribute (class option)         | Receives                         |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `lat-input` (`latInput`)         | the latitude                     |
| `lng-input` (`lngInput`)         | the longitude                    |
| `value-input` (`valueInput`)     | `"lat,lng"`                      |
| `address-input` (`addressInput`) | the address (`""` while unknown) |

- The bound inputs submit themselves; the picker never adds entries for them.
- Their initial values seed the picker when it has no `value`.
- They mirror the picker's events: a native `input` event for each live change, `input` + `change` on each commit, and nothing for silent writes (property writes, reset, restore). Their events are dispatched before the picker's own.
- Listeners on the input itself keep working: jQuery `$('#lat').on('change', …)`, Livewire `wire:model`, Alpine `x-model`.
- Clearing the value with a property write, a reset to an empty value or a restore sets them to `""` silently. They are never cleared at startup.

## Progressive enhancement (Laravel, Django, Rails)

Put the bound inputs inside the element:

- Without JavaScript they are visible and typed by hand.
- After the element upgrades they are no longer rendered, but they are still submitted, and the map writes them.
- Their server-rendered values seed the picker, even when the script runs in `<head>` before they are parsed.
- Their native events do not bubble, so a `change` listener on the picker only ever receives the picker's own `CustomEvent`.
- A form reset brings back the server values in the inputs and in the picker.

```blade
<form method="POST" action="{{ route('stores.update', $store) }}">
  @csrf
  @method('PUT')
  <label for="store-location">Store location</label>
  <location-picker id="store-location" lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" address-name="address"
                   required search reverse-geocode style="height: 360px">
    {{-- Without JS these are visible and typed by hand. With JS they are hidden, filled by the map, and still submitted.
         Their values seed the picker. No `required` here: the picker validates. --}}
    <input id="lat" name="lat" inputmode="decimal" value="{{ old('lat', $store->lat) }}" aria-label="Latitude">
    <input id="lng" name="lng" inputmode="decimal" value="{{ old('lng', $store->lng) }}" aria-label="Longitude">
  </location-picker>
  @error('lat') <p class="error">{{ $message }}</p> @enderror
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

```php
// StoreController@update
$data = $request->validate([
    'lat' => ['required', 'numeric', 'between:-90,90'],
    'lng' => ['required', 'numeric', 'between:-180,180'],
    'address' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255'],
]);
$store->update($data);
```

```django
{% load l10n %}
<location-picker lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" required search>
  <input id="lat" name="lat" value="{{ form.lat.value|default_if_none:''|unlocalize }}" aria-label="Latitude">
  <input id="lng" name="lng" value="{{ form.lng.value|default_if_none:''|unlocalize }}" aria-label="Longitude">
</location-picker>
```

`unlocalize` keeps Django from writing a decimal comma. Validate on the server too, for example with Django's `DecimalField(min_value=-90, max_value=90)` for latitude:

```python
from django import forms


class StoreForm(forms.Form):
    lat = forms.DecimalField(min_value=-90, max_value=90, decimal_places=6)
    lng = forms.DecimalField(min_value=-180, max_value=180, decimal_places=6)
```

Hidden inputs outside the element work the same way (the most common pattern in existing apps):

```html
<form method="post" action="/places">
  <input type="hidden" name="lat" id="lat" value="48.8584" />
  <input type="hidden" name="lng" id="lng" value="2.2945" />
  <location-picker lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" required style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

## Validation

- `required` reports `valueMissing` while the picker is unset, with the message "Please choose a location on the map." (`messages.valueMissing`). `reportValidity()` focuses the map.
- `setCustomValidity(message)` works as on native inputs.
- **Put `required` on the picker, never on hidden bound inputs.** A hidden, empty, `required` input blocks the submit as "not focusable", and the picker warns about it.
- `readonly` (zoom allowed, the value cannot change) and `disabled` bar the element from validation, as on native inputs.
- Style errors after the user interacted with `location-picker:state(interacted):invalid`. `:user-invalid` is not reliable on custom elements.
- `:required` and `:read-only` never work on form-associated custom elements. Use `location-picker[required]` and `location-picker[readonly]`.
- `center` is only where the view starts. It is never submitted; the user has to commit a point (pan, Enter, the confirm button, search, locate).

```html
<style>
  location-picker:state(interacted):invalid {
    outline: 2px solid crimson;
  }
  location-picker[required] {
    border-inline-start: 4px solid #1d4ed8;
  }
</style>
<form method="post" action="/places">
  <location-picker name="location" required center="48.8584,2.2945"></location-picker>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

## Reset and back/forward

- `form.reset()` returns the picker to its reset value: the `value` attribute, else the `lat` + `lng` attributes, else the bound inputs' server-rendered values, else unset. It then writes that value into the bound inputs. Nothing fires: no `input`, no `change`.
- Back/forward navigation (bfcache, history) restores the value, the zoom and the address, again silently.
- The dirty flag works like a native input: once the user (or a property write) changed the value, later changes to the `value`, `lat` or `lng` attributes only update the default. A `lat`/`lng` change ignored this way logs one warning. To control the value, bind the `value` property or call `setLocation()`.

## jQuery, AJAX, Livewire, Alpine, htmx

- **jQuery `.serialize()` ignores custom elements:** it only serializes `input`, `select` and `textarea`. Use bound inputs, or `new FormData(form)`.
- **Livewire and Alpine:** bind the inputs (`wire:model="lat"`, `x-model="lat"`) and point `lat-input`/`lng-input` at them.
- **Delegated listeners** (`$(form).on('change', 'input', …)`, htmx `hx-trigger="change"` on the form) do not see the native events of inputs nested in the picker, because those do not bubble. Listen to the picker's own `change` instead: `hx-trigger="change from:location-picker"`.

## Name collisions

If a `*-name` attribute equals the `name` of a bound input in the same form, the value would be submitted twice. The picker logs one warning ("use either lat-name or lat-input") and never changes your inputs.

## The JavaScript class in a form

`LocationPicker` is not a form control. In class mode, bind inputs with `latInput`/`lngInput`/`valueInput`/`addressInput`; their native events bubble normally.

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker';

const picker = new LocationPicker('#map', { latInput: '#lat', lngInput: '#lng', search: true });
picker.addEventListener('change', (e) => console.log(e.detail.value));
```

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/frameworks.md

# Frameworks

`<location-picker>` is a standard custom element, so every framework can render it. The rules are the same everywhere:

- **Bind `value`**, a `"lat,lng"` string (`""` while unset). Writing it is silent and idempotent, so bindings never loop.
- **Listen to `change`** for committed values, or **`input`** for live updates. Every commit fires `input` (final value) then `change`, so bindings that only listen to `input` still see search picks, locate results and `setLocation()`.
- **Spell configuration as HTML attributes** (`lat-name`, `api-key`, `reverse-geocode`). That is SSR-correct; the hyphen-less spellings (`latname`) are accepted too.
- **Never bind `lat`/`lng`** in a template: they only set the initial value.
- Objects (`messages`, `mapOptions`, `engine`, `geocoder`, `geolocation`) are properties, set from JavaScript.
- `import 'location-picker'` defines the element and is safe on the server (it does nothing there).

## Value binding

| Framework                         | Value binding                                                                                                  | Events                                                                                                           | Notes                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain `<form>`                    | FormData via ElementInternals                                                                                  | `change`, `input`                                                                                                | reset and bfcache restore handled                                                                                                   |
| React 19                          | `value={str}` (property)                                                                                       | `onChange`/`onInput` (synthetic); lowercase `onaddresschange`, `onready`, `onerror` (native; client render only) | `import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react'`; kebab-case config; after `hydrateRoot`, objects and native listeners go in a ref |
| Vue 3.5                           | `v-model` (`input` + `el.value`); `v-model.lazy` (`change`)                                                    | `@change`, `@addresschange`                                                                                      | `compilerOptions.isCustomElement`                                                                                                   |
| Angular 17+                       | `formControlName`/`ngModel` + **`ngDefaultControl`** (DefaultValueAccessor: `value` property, `input`, `blur`) | `(change)`, `(addresschange)`                                                                                    | `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`; no custom ControlValueAccessor needed                                                                     |
| Svelte 5                          | `value={v}`                                                                                                    | `onchange`, `onaddresschange`                                                                                    | `jsx/svelte` types                                                                                                                  |
| Solid                             | `prop:value`                                                                                                   | `on:change`                                                                                                      | `jsx/solid` types                                                                                                                   |
| jQuery / Livewire / Alpine / htmx | bound inputs (native events on the input itself) or `new FormData(form)`                                       | `change` on the picker for delegated or form-level listeners (htmx `hx-trigger="change from:location-picker"`)   | `.serialize()` ignores custom elements                                                                                              |

**Event names per framework.** The class callbacks `onChange`/`onInput`/`onAddressChange`/`onReady`/`onError` are options of the JavaScript class only.

| Framework | `change` | `input` | `addresschange` | `ready` | `error` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain JS | `addEventListener('change')` | `'input'` | `'addresschange'` | `'ready'` | `'error'` |
| React 19 | `onChange` | `onInput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` (NOT `onError`: React's synthetic `error` never fires for this element; a type error in `jsx/react`) |
| Vue 3 | `@change` | `@input` | `@addresschange` | `@ready` | `@error` |
| Angular | `(change)` | `(input)` | `(addresschange)` | `(ready)` | `(error)` |
| Svelte 5 | `onchange` | `oninput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` |
| Solid | `on:change` | `on:input` | `on:addresschange` | `on:ready` | `on:error` |
| Preact | `onchange` | `oninput` | `onaddresschange` | `onready` | `onerror` |

React's lowercase native handlers are attached on client render only. After `hydrateRoot`, use a ref (React hydration recipe below).

## React 19 and Next.js

Import `location-picker` in a client component, and the JSX typings once. React 19 sets `value`, `search`, `locate` and other props as properties when they exist on the element, and fires `onChange`/`onInput` for the element's events. React 18 sets attributes instead, so `value` binding needs React 19.

```tsx
'use client';
import 'location-picker';                          // defines <location-picker>; SSR-safe no-op on the server
import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react';   // JSX typings
import { useState } from 'react';

export function StoreLocationField({ initial = '' }: { initial?: string }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);    // "lat,lng" or ""
  // Attributes, value and onChange/onInput survive SSR hydration; objects (messages…) and onaddresschange go in a ref (recipe below).
  return (
    <>
      <label htmlFor="loc">Location</label>
      <location-picker id="loc" name="location" lat-name="lat" lng-name="lng" required search
        value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.currentTarget.value)} style={{ height: 360 }} />
      <p>{value || 'Pan the map to choose'}</p>
    </>
  );
}
// <form action={saveStore}>: formData.get('lat'), formData.get('lng'), formData.get('location')
```

**React hydration recipe.** With `hydrateRoot` (Next.js App Router, Remix), React applies neither object props (`messages`, `mapOptions`, `engine`, `geocoder`, `geolocation`, an adapter-object `provider`) nor the lowercase native handlers to custom elements. Set them in a ref callback; refs are attached on hydration. Attributes, `value` and `onChange`/`onInput` keep working.

```tsx
'use client';
import 'location-picker';
import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react';
import type { AddressDetail } from 'location-picker';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function AddressField() {
  const [address, setAddress] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <location-picker
        name="location"
        reverse-geocode
        ref={(el) => {
          if (!el) return;
          el.messages = { locate: 'Use my position' };
          const onAddress = (e: CustomEvent<AddressDetail>) => setAddress(e.detail.address);
          el.addEventListener('addresschange', onAddress);
          return () => el.removeEventListener('addresschange', onAddress);
        }}
      />
      <p>{address ?? 'No address yet'}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

- Use `onerror` (lowercase) for the picker's errors. `onError`, `onAddressChange` and `onReady` are type errors in `location-picker/jsx/react`: those names never fire for this element.
- In a Server Action, read `formData.get('location')` (or `lat`/`lng` with `lat-name`/`lng-name`).
- `<location-picker form="f1">` works in React 19: the `form` property writes the attribute.

## Vue 3 and Nuxt

Tell the compiler that `location-picker` is a custom element, then use `v-model` (live, `input`) or `v-model.lazy` (`change`).

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'location-picker' } } })],
});
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import 'location-picker';
import { ref } from 'vue';
const location = ref('');                         // v-model uses `input` + el.value; v-model.lazy uses `change`
const address = ref<string | null>(null);
</script>
<template>
  <label for="loc">Location</label>
  <location-picker id="loc" v-model="location" name="location" search reverse-geocode
                   @addresschange="address = $event.detail.address" style="height: 360px" />
  <p>{{ location || 'Pan the map to choose' }} <small v-if="address">{{ address }}</small></p>
</template>
```

In Nuxt, set the same compiler option in `nuxt.config.ts`. The import is safe during server rendering.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  vue: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'location-picker' } },
});
```

Types for templates: `import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/vue'`. The element keeps its state across `<KeepAlive>`.

## Angular 17+

Use `ngDefaultControl`: Angular's DefaultValueAccessor writes the `value` property and listens to `input` and `blur`, which is exactly what the element provides. No custom ControlValueAccessor is needed. Add `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`.

```ts
import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA } from '@angular/core';
import { FormControl, FormGroup, ReactiveFormsModule, Validators } from '@angular/forms';
import 'location-picker';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-store-form',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [ReactiveFormsModule],
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  template: `
    <form [formGroup]="form" (ngSubmit)="save()">
      <label for="loc">Location</label>
      <location-picker id="loc" formControlName="location" ngDefaultControl search locate="button" style="height:360px"></location-picker>
      @if (form.controls.location.touched && form.controls.location.invalid) { <p>Choose a location.</p> }
      <button [disabled]="form.invalid">Save</button>
    </form>`,
})
export class StoreFormComponent {
  form = new FormGroup({ location: new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true, validators: [Validators.required] }) });
  save() { const [lat, lng] = this.form.getRawValue().location.split(',').map(Number); console.log({ lat, lng }); }
}
```

- `[(ngModel)]` works the same way with `ngDefaultControl`.
- Listen to `(addresschange)="onAddress($event)"` for the address.
- With bound inputs nested inside the element, the control still holds `"lat,lng"`: the inputs' own events do not bubble to the host.

## Svelte 5

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import 'location-picker';
  import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/svelte';
  let location = $state('');
</script>

<label for="loc">Location</label>
<location-picker id="loc" name="location" search value={location}
  onchange={(e) => (location = e.detail.value)} style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
<p>{location || 'Pan the map to choose'}</p>
```

## Solid

```tsx
import 'location-picker';
import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/solid';
import { createSignal } from 'solid-js';

export function LocationField() {
  const [location, setLocation] = createSignal('');
  return (
    <location-picker name="location" search prop:value={location()}
      on:change={(e) => setLocation(e.detail.value)} style={{ height: '360px' }} />
  );
}
```

## Preact

```tsx
/** @jsxImportSource preact */
import 'location-picker';
import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/preact';
import { useState } from 'preact/hooks';

export function LocationField() {
  const [location, setLocation] = useState('');
  return (
    <location-picker name="location" search value={location}
      onchange={(e) => setLocation(e.detail.value)} style={{ height: '360px' }} />
  );
}
```

## Astro and other server-rendered pages

Render the tag in the page and load the script on the client. In Astro, a `<script>` that imports the package is bundled for the browser:

```astro
<form method="post">
  <location-picker name="location" required style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script>
  import 'location-picker';
</script>
```

Templates without a bundler (Laravel Blade, Django, Rails ERB, Express views) use the script tag and bound inputs: see [forms.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/forms.md).

## jQuery, Livewire, Alpine and htmx

These libraries listen on inputs, so give the picker bound inputs and let them receive native `input` and `change` events:

```html
<form method="post" action="/places">
  <input type="hidden" name="lat" id="lat" /><input type="hidden" name="lng" id="lng" />
  <location-picker lat-input="lat" lng-input="lng" required style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
<script>
  document
    .getElementById('lat')
    .addEventListener('change', (e) => console.log('lat', e.target.value));
</script>
```

- jQuery: `$('#lat').on('change', …)` fires. `$(form).serialize()` skips the picker itself, so submit bound inputs or `new FormData(form)`.
- Livewire: `<input type="hidden" id="lat" wire:model="lat">`. Alpine: `x-model="lat"` on the input.
- htmx: `hx-trigger="change from:location-picker"`.

## TypeScript

- `document.querySelector('location-picker')` is typed as `LocationPickerElement` (the package augments `HTMLElementTagNameMap`).
- JSX and template typings are opt-in: `import type {} from 'location-picker/jsx/react'` (or `preact`, `solid`, `vue`, `svelte`). They type the attributes, the `locate` modes and the event handlers.
- `instanceof` can differ when two copies of the library are on one page (for example the ESM and the script build). Check with `customElements.get('location-picker')` or duck typing instead.

## Component tests in jsdom or happy-dom

jsdom and happy-dom lack parts of the platform the element needs (form internals, `ResizeObserver`, constructable stylesheets). There the element runs **inert**: it never throws, it logs one console message naming the missing API, and `value`, `valueAsLatLng` and `setLocation()` still round-trip, so components that render a picker can be unit tested. Test maps and form submission in a real browser.

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/providers.md

# Providers, geocoders and usage policies

A provider is the map engine: `leaflet` (the default, OpenStreetMap, no key), `google` or `maplibre`. Each provider has a paired geocoder for the search box and for reverse geocoding.

| Provider   | Engine                              | Loaded how                                               | Search and reverse geocoding                |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `leaflet`  | Leaflet 1.9.4 + OpenStreetMap tiles | `window.L`, or auto-loaded from jsDelivr with SRI        | Photon                                      |
| `google`   | Google Maps JavaScript API          | already on the page, or Google's bootstrap with your key | `PlaceAutocompleteElement`, Google Geocoder |
| `maplibre` | `maplibre-gl` + OpenFreeMap style   | bring your own (never auto-loaded)                       | Photon                                      |

## How the provider is chosen

1. An explicit `provider` wins: a name (`provider="google"`) or an adapter object (`provider: leafletProvider({ … })`). The aliases `osm` and `openstreetmap` (for `leaflet`) and `googlemaps` and `google-maps` (for `google`) work with a warning. Any other name is an `INVALID_OPTION` error: no map is created and `ready` rejects.
2. Otherwise a Google-only signal selects `google`: `api-key`, `map-id`, `marker="advanced"`, the deprecated `useAdvancedMarker`, or a 3rd constructor argument.
3. Otherwise `leaflet`. A `google.maps` global already on the page is never used by accident; it only triggers a one-time console hint.

MapLibre is never inferred: ask for it with `provider="maplibre"`. `lat`/`lng` are not a Google signal.

String providers are loaded lazily as separate chunks (the script build bundles all three). Adapter objects are imported statically and let `picker.map` exist synchronously. Options passed to the adapter factory win over the picker's own options.

## Leaflet and OpenStreetMap (default)

**Engine.** The adapter uses, in order: the `engine` option (`import * as L from 'leaflet'`), then `window.L`, then auto-loads `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js` with Subresource Integrity (`crossorigin="anonymous"` and your CSP nonce), once per page. `engine-url` points the auto-load somewhere else (no integrity check for custom URLs); `engine-url="none"` never loads anything and reports `ENGINE_MISSING` when `L` is absent. Leaflet 2 works through `engine`; the auto-load stays on 1.9.4.

RequireJS or AMD pages must load Leaflet before RequireJS, or pass `engine`, because Leaflet's UMD build calls an anonymous `define()`.

**Leaflet's CSS** is resolved without a forced download when your page already has it:

1. `engine-css-url` set to a URL: that stylesheet is linked.
2. The adapter auto-loaded Leaflet: the pinned `leaflet.css` is linked with integrity.
3. Readable `leaflet.css` rules on the page (for example `import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css'` in a bundle) are used; for the element they are copied into its shadow root.
4. Otherwise the pinned `leaflet.css` is linked from jsDelivr (skipped with `engine-css-url="none"`).
5. After mounting, the picker checks that the CSS applied, and reports `ENGINE_CSS_MISSING` (a warning) with a fix if not.

The map never waits for the CSS, so a bundled `L` gives you `picker.map` synchronously.

**Tiles.** The default is `https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`, maximum zoom 19, with the "© OpenStreetMap contributors" credit always visible (the attribution is forced while the default tiles are used). OpenStreetMap's tiles are a shared community service with a [tile usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/): keep the attribution visible, do not bulk-download, and expect best-effort availability with no SLA. For production traffic, use your own or a commercial tile server:

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker';

const picker = new LocationPicker('#map', {
  tileUrl: 'https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png',
  attribution: '&copy; Example Maps &copy; OpenStreetMap contributors',
  maxZoom: 20,
});
```

On the element that is `tile-url="…" attribution="…" max-zoom="20"`. Changing `tile-url` swaps the layer without rebuilding the map. A custom `tile-url` without `attribution` logs a warning.

**Self-hosted Leaflet** (no CDN, for strict CSP):

```html
<location-picker name="location" engine-url="/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.js"
  engine-css-url="/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.css" style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
<script src="/vendor/location-picker/location-picker.global.js"></script>
```

**Gestures.** Zoom is anchored at the pin (wheel, double-click and pinch), so zooming never changes the value. With `gesture-handling="auto"` (the default), a page that scrolls gets cooperative gestures: a plain wheel scrolls the page and shows "Use Ctrl + scroll to zoom the map" (⌘ on Apple platforms); one finger still pans the map. `greedy` always zooms, `none` disables gestures (buttons and keys only).

## Google Maps

Google is used only when you ask: `provider="google"`, or a key, a map ID or `marker="advanced"`.

**Loading.** The adapter uses, in order: the `engine` option (a `google.maps` namespace); a `google.maps.Map` already on the page (a classic `<script src="https://maps.googleapis.com/…">` page, mounted immediately); `google.maps.importLibrary`; and finally, when `api-key` is set, Google's official inline bootstrap, injected once per page with your key, `v=weekly`, the page language and your CSP nonce. With none of these you get `API_KEY_MISSING`.

**Your key.** Create a browser key, restrict it by HTTP referrer, and enable the Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New) for `search`, and the Geocoding API only for `reverse-geocode` or `lookupAddress()`. A rejected key (referrer restrictions, billing, a disabled API) is reported as `GOOGLE_AUTH_FAILED` on every Google picker on the page; an existing `window.gm_authFailure` handler is still called.

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core';
import { googleProvider } from 'location-picker/google';

const picker = new LocationPicker<google.maps.Map>('#map', {
  provider: googleProvider({
    apiKey: 'YOUR_BROWSER_KEY',
    region: 'LB',
    mapOptions: { mapTypeId: 'hybrid' },
  }),
  search: true,
  locate: 'button',
});
const map = (await picker.ready).map;
```

To control loading yourself, `loadGoogleMaps({ apiKey })` injects the same bootstrap and resolves with the `google.maps` namespace.

**The pin** is a CSS overlay, so no Marker and no map ID are needed. `marker="advanced"` draws an `AdvancedMarkerElement` instead; it needs `map-id`, and without one the CSS pin stays and `MAP_ID_REQUIRED` is reported.

**Zoom.** Wheel, double-click and the zoom control are re-anchored at the pin, so they never change the value. A pinch on Google Maps zooms around the fingers, so the centre moves and the new centre is committed (source `user`).

**Search** uses Google's `PlaceAutocompleteElement` (never the legacy `places.Autocomplete`). A picked place moves the map and commits with its formatted address. Pasting coordinates (`48.85, 2.29`, a Google Maps URL) into the box jumps there without a Places request.

**Terms.** The [Google Maps Platform Terms of Service](https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) do not allow Google Maps content, such as Places results or Geocoding addresses, on or next to a non-Google map. The picker therefore pairs geocoders with providers and refuses a mismatch (`GEOCODER_MISMATCH`), and when an element switches between Google and another provider it clears the address. If you write a custom geocoder for a Google map, its results must come from Google.

**Colours.** Google's `colorScheme` follows the element's computed `color-scheme` at mount.

## MapLibre

MapLibre GL is bring-your-own: the library never downloads `maplibre-gl` or its CSS by default. The default style is OpenFreeMap's keyless `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` ([OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org/)).

```ts
import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl';
import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css';
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core';
import { maplibreProvider } from 'location-picker/maplibre';

const picker = new LocationPicker('#map', { provider: maplibreProvider({ engine: maplibregl }), search: true });
```

Without a bundler, load the engine yourself and give it to the element:

```html
<location-picker provider="maplibre" name="location" style="height: 360px"
  engine-css-url="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@6/dist/maplibre-gl.css"></location-picker>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
<script type="module">
  import * as maplibregl from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/maplibre-gl@6/+esm';
  document.querySelector('location-picker').engine = maplibregl;
</script>
```

- **CSS:** readable MapLibre CSS on the page is used (and copied into the element's shadow root). Otherwise nothing is fetched and `ENGINE_CSS_MISSING` (a warning) tells you to `import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'` or set `engine-css-url`.
- **Engine URL:** `engine-url` set to an ES module URL is loaded with `import()`. That is opt-in and cannot use Subresource Integrity.
- **Style:** `map-style` takes a style URL; the `mapStyle` property also takes a style object. Setting only `tile-url` wraps an XYZ raster template into a style.
- Rotation and pitch are off and zoom is anchored at the pin. `cooperative` maps to MapLibre's `cooperativeGestures`.
- MapLibre's worker needs `worker-src blob:` under a Content Security Policy ([csp.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/csp.md)).

## Geocoders

| Provider              | Paired geocoder                                 | `pairsWith`               |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `leaflet`, `maplibre` | `photonGeocoder()`                              | `['leaflet', 'maplibre']` |
| `google`              | `googleGeocoder()` + `PlaceAutocompleteElement` | `['google']`              |

Search and reverse geocoding are off until you set `search` or `reverse-geocode` (or call `geocode()` / `lookupAddress()`). Coordinates never need a geocoder: in the built-in search box (Leaflet and MapLibre), typed or pasted coordinates show one offline "Go to …" option, and on Google a pasted coordinate jumps directly.

### Photon

[Photon](https://photon.komoot.io/) (by komoot) is a keyless OpenStreetMap geocoder that supports search-as-you-type. The public endpoint is free under fair use, with no SLA, and heavy use is throttled. The picker is gentle with it: queries need 3 characters, are debounced by at least 300 ms on the public endpoint, cancel the previous request, are cached (100 searches, 200 reverse lookups) and return 5 results biased to the map centre. Reverse lookups run 400 ms after a commit.

For production, self-host Photon or use a commercial Photon endpoint:

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker';
import { photonGeocoder } from 'location-picker/photon';

new LocationPicker('#map', {
  search: true,
  reverseGeocode: true,
  geocoder: photonGeocoder({
    url: 'https://photon.example.org/api',
    reverseUrl: 'https://photon.example.org/reverse',
    params: { osm_tag: 'place' },
  }),
});
```

On the element, set the property: `el.geocoder = photonGeocoder({ url })`. With the script build, the factory is `LocationPicker.photonGeocoder`.

### Custom geocoders

A geocoder is an object with `search` and/or `reverse` (a bare function acts as `search`). Declare `pairsWith` so it is only used with maps it may appear on:

```ts
import { LocationPicker, type Geocoder, type GeocodeResult } from 'location-picker';

// For example, your own server-side endpoint in front of a commercial geocoder.
const myGeocoder: Geocoder = {
  pairsWith: ['leaflet', 'maplibre'],
  async search(query, { signal, near, limit, lang }) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({
      q: query,
      lat: String(near.lat),
      lng: String(near.lng),
      limit: String(limit),
      lang,
    });
    const response = await fetch(`/api/geocode?${params}`, { signal });
    return (await response.json()) as GeocodeResult[];
  },
  async reverse({ lat, lng }, { signal, lang }) {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reverse?lat=${lat}&lng=${lng}&lang=${lang}`, { signal });
    return (await response.json()) as GeocodeResult | null;
  },
};

new LocationPicker('#map', { search: true, reverseGeocode: true, geocoder: myGeocoder });
```

A geocoder without `pairsWith` works with every provider; then you are responsible for its terms, and non-Google results must never appear on a Google map. `geocoder: false` turns geocoding off (`geocode()` and `lookupAddress()` then reject with `GEOCODER_MISSING`).

Nominatim is never a default here and has no example in these docs. Its usage policy, https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/, forbids client-side autocomplete, allows at most one request per second and requires caching; read it before writing a custom geocoder that calls Nominatim, and do not use it for the search box.

## Switching providers on the element

Setting `provider`, `api-key`, `map-id`, `map-style`, `engine-url`, `engine-css-url`, `marker="advanced"`, `engine` or `mapOptions` rebuilds the map (several changes in one task rebuild once). The coordinates are kept, `el.ready` is replaced immediately, and `ready` fires again:

```ts
const el = document.querySelector('location-picker')!;
el.provider = 'google';
el.apiKey = 'YOUR_BROWSER_KEY';
const ready = await el.ready;
console.log(ready.map);
```

When the provider name changes (for example from `google` to `leaflet`), the address is cleared silently, so Google text never stays next to an OpenStreetMap map. With `reverse-geocode` on, the new provider's geocoder looks the address up again.

## Your own engine

Any map library can be plugged in through the public `ProviderAdapter` contract. An OpenLayers adapter in about 20 lines:

```ts
import { LocationPicker, type ProviderAdapter } from 'location-picker/core';
import OlMap from 'ol/Map'; import View from 'ol/View'; import TileLayer from 'ol/layer/Tile'; import OSM from 'ol/source/OSM';
import { fromLonLat, toLonLat } from 'ol/proj';

const openlayers: ProviderAdapter<OlMap> = {
  name: 'openlayers',
  mount({ container, view, events, signal }) {
    const map = new OlMap({ target: container, layers: [new TileLayer({ source: new OSM() })],
      view: new View({ center: fromLonLat([view.center.lng, view.center.lat]), zoom: view.zoom }) });
    const center = () => { const [lng, lat] = toLonLat(map.getView().getCenter()!); return { lat, lng }; };
    map.getView().on('change:center', () => events.move(center()));
    map.on('moveend', () => { events.moveEnd(center(), map.getView().getZoom()!); events.interactionEnd(); });
    container.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => events.interactionStart(), { capture: true, signal });
    return {
      map, getCenter: center, getZoom: () => map.getView().getZoom()!,
      setView: (c, z, { animate }) => map.getView().animate({ center: fromLonLat([c.lng, c.lat]), zoom: z, duration: animate ? 250 : 0 }),
      setZoom: (z) => map.getView().setZoom(z),
      setInteractive: (m) => map.getInteractions().forEach((i) => i.setActive(m === 'full')),
      resize: () => map.updateSize(), destroy: () => map.setTarget(undefined),
    };
  },
};
new LocationPicker('#map', { provider: openlayers, value: '48.8584,2.2945' });
```

The adapter creates its map inside `container` only, reports camera changes through `events`, and the core does rounding, de-duplication and event sources. The member reference is in [api.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/api.md#provideradapter).

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/csp.md

# Content Security Policy

location-picker is built to run under a strict Content Security Policy:

- **Its own CSS needs no `style-src` entry.** The element adopts one constructed stylesheet into its shadow root, and the class adopts one into its target's document (or shadow root). Neither uses `style=""` attributes or inline `<style>` (except the fallback described below).
- **Everything it inserts carries your nonce**: the Leaflet `<script>` and `<link>`, Google's bootstrap, and the fallback `<style>`. The nonce comes from the `nonce` attribute or option, or by default from the first `script[nonce]` in the document.
- **It loads nothing you did not ask for.** By default that is Leaflet from jsDelivr (only when `window.L` is absent) and the OpenStreetMap tiles. Search and reverse geocoding add Photon. MapLibre and its CSS are never fetched unless you set a URL.

## Recipes

| Setup                                                                           | `script-src`                                                 | `style-src`                                                                                      | `img-src`                                              | `connect-src`                   | Other                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Default: Leaflet auto-load + OSM                                                | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` (or `'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'`) | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net`                                                                       | `https://tile.openstreetmap.org`                       | –                               | –                                      |
| + `search` / `reverse-geocode` (Photon)                                         | as above                                                     | as above                                                                                         | as above                                               | `https://photon.komoot.io`      | –                                      |
| Self-hosted engine (`engine-url="/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.js"`) or a bundled `L` | `'self'`                                                     | `'self'`                                                                                         | your tile host                                         | your Photon host                | –                                      |
| MapLibre (bundled) + OpenFreeMap                                                | `'self'`                                                     | `'self'` (or jsDelivr, only if you set `engine-css-url` to it)                                   | `'self' data: blob:`                                   | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org` | `worker-src blob:` (MapLibre's worker) |
| Google                                                                          | per Google's guide (nonce + `'strict-dynamic'`)              | Google injects `<style>` into the page and into the element's shadow root: follow Google's guide | `https://*.googleapis.com https://*.gstatic.com data:` | `https://*.googleapis.com`      | follow Google's guide for fonts        |
| Class mode where `adoptedStyleSheets` is unavailable                            | –                                                            | `'nonce-…'` (the fallback `<style nonce>`), or `injectStyles: false` + `style.css`               | –                                                      | –                               | –                                      |

If you load location-picker itself from jsDelivr (`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3`), that is already covered by the `script-src` entry of the default row. Self-hosting the script build means `'self'`.

## Examples

The default setup, with search, loading everything from jsDelivr:

```text
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; img-src 'self' https://tile.openstreetmap.org; connect-src 'self' https://photon.komoot.io
```

The same with a nonce instead of host allowlists (`RANDOM` is a fresh value per response, also set on your own `<script nonce="RANDOM">` tags):

```text
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-RANDOM' 'strict-dynamic'; style-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; img-src 'self' https://tile.openstreetmap.org; connect-src 'self' https://photon.komoot.io; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'
```

Everything self-hosted, with your own tiles and Photon:

```text
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' https://tiles.example.com; connect-src 'self' https://photon.example.org
```

```html
<location-picker
  name="location"
  search
  engine-url="/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.js"
  engine-css-url="/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.css"
  tile-url="https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
  attribution="&copy; OpenStreetMap contributors"
></location-picker>
```

With a bundler, pass the engine and import Leaflet's CSS yourself; nothing is fetched from a CDN (see the [JavaScript class example](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/README.md#javascript-class)).

## Class mode and `style.css`

The class adopts its stylesheet into the target's root node. Where constructable stylesheets are unavailable it falls back to a `<style>` element that carries the nonce. To add no styles at runtime at all, turn injection off and import the stylesheet from your bundle:

```ts
import 'location-picker/style.css';
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core';

new LocationPicker('#map', { injectStyles: false });
```

`location-picker/style.css` also contains a placeholder rule that reserves 320px for `<location-picker>` before the script runs, which avoids layout shift.

## Google Maps

Google's Maps JavaScript API has its own requirements, which change over time. Follow Google's [Content Security Policy guide](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/content-security-policy) (a nonce with `'strict-dynamic'`). The picker puts your nonce on the bootstrap script it injects, so Google's loader picks it up.

## Trusted Types

The engine auto-loader does not support `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` in 3.0. Load the engine yourself (a bundled `L` or your own `<script>`) and set `engine-url="none"`.

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/migration.md

# Migrating to v3

v3 keeps every v1 and v2 entry point working, but the new API is built around a form field: `<location-picker>` plus an imperative `LocationPicker` class, on OpenStreetMap by default. This page lists every v1 and v2 API, what happens to it, and the one-line fixes.

## Which path are you on?

| You use                                                                                      | What to do                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<script src="https://unpkg.com/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js">` (unpinned v1) | Nothing. Since 2.1.0 that path serves a frozen copy of v1 again. To get v3, follow [v1 script tag to v3](#v1-script-tag-to-v3). |
| npm 1.x: `import locationPicker from 'location-picker'`                                      | Change the import to `location-picker/v1`. Behaviour is identical.                                                              |
| npm 1.x CommonJS: `new (require('location-picker'))(…)`                                      | `require('location-picker/v1')`.                                                                                                |
| npm 2.x: `import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker'` with Google Maps                 | Pass `provider: googleProvider()` (or an `apiKey`). See [v2 to v3](#v2-to-v3).                                                  |
| A vendored copy of the v1 file                                                               | Nothing; it keeps working. v1 and v3 can run on the same page.                                                                  |

The frozen v1 file shares no code with v3. It only gained three bug fixes: longitude is wrapped into [-180, 180), latitude is clamped (#12), and `0` is a valid `lat`/`lng` (#11). The pin is an SVG with the same 28×44 footprint and anchor as the old PNG.

## Every v1 and v2 API

| v1 (1.1.1) / v2 (2.0.0) API | v3 | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `<script src=…/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js>`; global `locationPicker`; AMD | The same path serves the **frozen v1 file** (standalone source) | **Kept forever.** The 42 unpinned unpkg sites work again from 2.1.0 (D17) |
| `new locationPicker(el, {setCurrentPosition, lat, lng}, mapOptions)`; sync Google `.map`; `.element`; auto CSS; `.location-picker .centerMarker` 28×44; Tripoli; zoom 15 | Frozen v1 file. npm users: `import locationPicker from 'location-picker/v1'` | Kept. The only fixes are lng wrap/lat clamp (#12) and 0 as a valid lat/lng (#11) |
| `google.maps.event.addListener(lp.map,'idle',…)` | v1 file: unchanged. v3: `change` events (or `idle` on `picker.map` with `provider: googleProvider()`) | Kept / superseded |
| `new (require('location-picker'))()` (v1 CJS) | `require('location-picker/v1')` | Alias (one-line change) |
| `import LocationPicker from 'location-picker'` / `{ LocationPicker }` (v2) | Same names; `default` = v3 class | Kept |
| `require('location-picker')` → `{ LocationPicker, default }` (v2) | Same shape | Kept |
| v2 ctor `(element, options, mapOptions)` | Same signature. The 3rd argument merges into `mapOptions` and selects `google` (deprecation warning) | Kept |
| `getMarkerPosition()` | Same. Normalised, never a fake `{0,0}`. While unset it returns the view centre and warns once (read `valueAsLatLng`) | Kept (bug fixed) |
| `setLocation(lat, lng)` | Same, plus a `LatLngInput` overload; now commits (`change`, source `api`). Out-of-range latitude is clamped with a warning, as Google clamped it in v2 (D19) | Kept |
| `setCurrentPosition()` (v1 void / v2 Promise) | Alias of `locate()` that keeps the current zoom, like v2 (`locate()` itself zooms to max(current, 17)): `Promise<LocationDetail>` (⊇ LatLng). Rejects `LocationPickerError` with `.code`; never hangs | Kept (v2 shape) |
| Option `setCurrentPosition` (default **true**) | `locate: 'auto'` when `true`. The default is now `'off'` | **Default changed** (LOCKED 7) |
| Options `lat`, `lng` | Deprecated aliases of `value` (both required; 0 valid; latitude clamped with a warning, D19; NOT a provider signal) | Alias |
| `onLocationChange(pos)` | Called like `onChange` (de-duplicated; the detail is a superset of LatLng). Like v2's first `idle`, also called ONCE after `ready` with the current value (source `api`), but only when a value is set: v2 always had a position (Tripoli or geolocation), while an unset v3 picker has none, and reporting the 20,0 world view would fill hidden inputs with a fake location | **Changed** (not called after `ready` while unset) |
| `useAdvancedMarker` | `marker: 'advanced'` (Google; needs `mapId`, else `MAP_ID_REQUIRED` + CSS pin); also selects `google` | Alias |
| `destroy()` | Removes the created map, every listener and every node | Kept (bug fixed) |
| `import 'location-picker/style.css'` | Still exported (now optional: auto-adopt is the default), with a types stub | Kept |
| `.map` (sync `google.maps.Map`, v1/v2) | `undefined` until `ready`; SYNC with `provider: googleProvider()` on a page with classic Google loaded | **Break** (one-line fix) |
| Implicit Google provider (v2) | Google is selected by `apiKey`/`mapId`/`useAdvancedMarker`/3rd argument. Otherwise OSM, with a console hint | **Break** (zero public v2 users found) |
| Tripoli fallback | World view (20, 0) at zoom 2, unset | Removed (#7); kept in the v1 file |
| `.centerMarker` / PNG pin | Class mode: `.lp-pin.centerMarker` (alias kept). Element: `::part(pin)`. SVG + CSS variables | Changed (the v1 file keeps the PNG/SVG v1 look) |
| v2 d.ts (global `google`, CSS import, extensionless specifiers) | Fixed per LOCKED 10 | Fixed (#2) |
| `"type": "module"`, `engines.node >= 18` | `"type": "commonjs"` with `.mjs`/`.cjs`; no `engines` | Changed (deep `.mjs`/`.cjs` paths kept) |
| GPL `LICENSE` text | MIT; the README/CHANGELOG grant MIT for all prior versions too | Fixed (LOCKED 1) |

(D17, D19, LOCKED 1, 7 and 10 refer to decisions in the v3 design record; the table is copied from it unchanged.)

## Breaks, changed defaults and changed behaviour

- **`.map` is `undefined` until `ready`** (Break). v1 and v2 created the Google map synchronously in the constructor. In v3 the engine loads first. Wait for `await picker.ready`, use the `ready` event, or pass an adapter object on a page that already loaded Google Maps with a classic script tag: then `picker.map` is set before the constructor returns.
- **Google is no longer implicit** (Break). Without `provider: 'google'`, `apiKey`, `mapId`, `useAdvancedMarker` or a 3rd constructor argument, v3 uses OpenStreetMap. A loaded `google.maps` global is never sniffed; it only triggers a one-time console hint.
- **No location prompt on load** (Default changed). The `setCurrentPosition` option defaulted to `true` in v1 and v2. In v3 the locate control defaults to `'off'`; `setCurrentPosition: true` still maps to `locate: 'auto'`. Prefer `locate: 'button'`, which prompts only when clicked.
- **`onLocationChange`** (Changed) is called like `onChange`, plus once after `ready` when a value is set. An unset picker does not report the world view as a position.
- **The pin** (Changed) is an SVG themed with `--lp-pin-color`, `--lp-pin-size` and friends. In class mode it keeps the `centerMarker` class, so `.location-picker .centerMarker { display: none }` still hides it. On the element, use `location-picker::part(pin)`.
- **Package format** (Changed): `"type": "commonjs"` with `.mjs`/`.cjs` files and no `engines` field. `import` and `require` resolve as before.
- **The Tripoli fallback is gone** (Removed). With no `value` and no `center`, v3 shows a world view and stays unset.
- **`setLocation()` commits**: it fires `input` and `change` (source `api`).
- **`getMarkerPosition()` while unset** returns the view centre and warns once. Read the user's choice from `value` (`""` while unset) or `valueAsLatLng` (`null` while unset).

## v1 script tag to v3

v1 pages typically created the picker, listened for Google's `idle` event and copied the position into hidden inputs:

```html
<div id="map" style="height: 400px"></div>
<input type="hidden" name="lat" id="lat" /><input type="hidden" name="lng" id="lng" />
<script src="https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js?key=YOUR_BROWSER_KEY"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js"></script>
<script>
  var lp = new locationPicker('map', { setCurrentPosition: true }, { zoom: 15 });
  google.maps.event.addListener(lp.map, 'idle', function () {
    var p = lp.getMarkerPosition();
    document.getElementById('lat').value = p.lat;
    document.getElementById('lng').value = p.lng;
  });
</script>
```

In v3 the element fills the same inputs itself, on OpenStreetMap with no key, and the locate button replaces the automatic prompt:

```html
<form method="post" action="/places">
  <location-picker
    lat-input="lat"
    lng-input="lng"
    locate="button"
    required
    style="height: 400px"
  ></location-picker>
  <input type="hidden" name="lat" id="lat" /><input type="hidden" name="lng" id="lng" />
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

To stay on Google Maps, add `provider="google" api-key="YOUR_BROWSER_KEY"` (see [providers.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/providers.md#google-maps)).

## v2 to v3

The class keeps its v2 name, constructor signature and methods. Map the options:

| v2                                       | v3                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `setCurrentPosition: true` (the default) | `locate: 'auto'`, or better `locate: 'button'`                           |
| `lat: 45.5, lng: -73.56`                 | `value: { lat: 45.5, lng: -73.56 }` or `value: '45.5,-73.56'`            |
| `onLocationChange: (p) => …`             | `onChange: (detail) => …` (`detail` has `lat`, `lng`, `value`, `source`) |
| `useAdvancedMarker: true`                | `marker: 'advanced'` with `mapId` (Google only)                          |
| 3rd argument `{ zoom: 3, … }`            | `zoom: 3` and `mapOptions: { … }`, with `provider: 'google'`             |
| implicit Google                          | `provider: googleProvider()` or `apiKey`                                 |
| `import 'location-picker/style.css'`     | optional; styles are adopted automatically                               |

A v2 Google picker that needs `picker.map` right away:

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker/core';
import { googleProvider } from 'location-picker/google';

const picker = new LocationPicker<google.maps.Map>('map', {
  provider: googleProvider(),
  value: { lat: 45.5, lng: -73.56 },
  locate: 'button',
  onChange: (d) => console.log(d.source, d.lat, d.lng),
});
picker.map?.setOptions({ mapTypeId: 'hybrid' }); // set synchronously when Google Maps is already loaded
```

The same picker on OpenStreetMap, without a key:

```ts
import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker';

const picker = new LocationPicker('#map', {
  value: '45.5,-73.56',
  locate: 'button',
  onChange: (d) => console.log(d.value),
});
await picker.ready;
```

`setCurrentPosition()` still returns a promise, now with a `LocationDetail`. It rejects with a `LocationPickerError` whose `code` is `GEOLOCATION_DENIED`, `GEOLOCATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `GEOLOCATION_TIMEOUT`, `GEOLOCATION_UNSUPPORTED` or `ABORTED`, and it never hangs.

## v1 and v3 on the same page

The frozen v1 file defines the lowercase global `locationPicker`; the v3 script build defines `LocationPicker` and `<location-picker>`. Both can be loaded on one page, so a site can migrate one form at a time.

From 2.1.0 the package ships the MIT License text, and the author grants the MIT License for all prior versions of location-picker as well.

# Troubleshooting

Problems are reported loudly. Failures fire an `error` event whose detail is a `LocationPickerError` with a stable `code` and a one-line `fix`; if nothing handles the event, it is logged as `[location-picker] <what happened>. Fix: <fix>`. Configuration slips (unknown options, misspelled attributes, a clamped latitude) are one-time `console.warn` lines. Every error code and its fix is listed in [errors.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/errors.md).

To handle errors yourself, listen for `error` and call `preventDefault()` to stop the console log, or pass an `onError` callback to the class:

```html
<location-picker id="loc" name="location"></location-picker>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
<script>
  document.getElementById('loc').addEventListener('error', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault(); // handled here, so it is not logged
    console.warn(e.detail.code, e.detail.fix);
  });
</script>
```

Promises (`ready`, `locate()`, `geocode()`, `lookupAddress()`) reject with the same error type instead of firing `error`.

## `<location-picker>` stays empty

- **Only `location-picker/core` was imported.** `core` is the side-effect-free class. `import 'location-picker'` (or `location-picker/element`, or the script tag) defines the element.
- **The script URL is the v1 file.** `…/location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js` without a version is the frozen v1 build, which defines the global `locationPicker` and no element. Use `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3`.
- **The engine failed to load** (`ENGINE_LOAD_FAILED`, `ENGINE_MISSING`, `API_KEY_MISSING`). The picker then shows an error message and a text input for typing coordinates, so the form stays usable. Put your own content in `slot="error"`.

## The map is grey, blank or unstyled

- **Leaflet's CSS did not apply** (`ENGINE_CSS_MISSING`). Load `leaflet.css` on the page, set `engine-css-url`, or allow `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` in your CSP `style-src` ([csp.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/csp.md)).
- **Tiles are blocked.** Check the network panel and your CSP `img-src`. Tile failures leave the map interactive, and commits still work.
- **The class target has no height.** A `LocationPicker` target that measures 0 px tall gets `min-block-size: 320px` and a one-time warning. Give it a height. The element is 320px tall by default.
- **Inside tabs, a `<dialog>` or `display: none`.** Nothing to do: the picker resizes and re-centres on the value when it becomes visible.

## `locationPicker is not defined` or `LocationPicker is not defined`

The lowercase `locationPicker` global belongs to the v1 file (`dist/location-picker.min.js`). The v3 script build (`location-picker@3`) defines `LocationPicker` (capital L) and the `<location-picker>` element. Both can be on one page.

## Nothing is submitted

- Give the picker a `name` (or `lat-name`/`lng-name`), or bind existing inputs with `lat-input`/`lng-input`.
- A `disabled` picker, or one inside `<fieldset disabled>`, submits nothing, like any input.
- jQuery `.serialize()` skips custom elements. Use bound inputs or `new FormData(form)`.
- An unset picker submits an empty value (`location=`). Add `required` to make the user choose.

## The form does not submit, and the browser complains about a control that is "not focusable"

A hidden input has `required`. Remove it and put `required` on `<location-picker>`.

## The value ignores my `lat`/`lng` bindings

`lat` and `lng` set the initial value only. Once the control is dirty (any pan, commit or `value` write, including the `el.value = ''` that Vue `v-model` and Angular `writeValue` perform on mount), changing them is ignored with the warning "lat/lng only set the initial value; bind value="lat,lng" or call setLocation()". Bind `value` instead.

## The value looks swapped or clamped

- Everything is **latitude first**. `"2.2945,48.8584"` is a valid point in the Indian Ocean, not Paris; the picker cannot detect that swap.
- A string with a latitude outside [-90, 90] is rejected with `INVALID_VALUE` and a hint such as `did you swap lat and lng? try "45,120"`.
- Numbers and objects are clamped instead: `setLocation(95, 10)` commits `"90,10"` and warns "latitude 95 was clamped to 90; did you swap lat and lng? try (10, 95)".
- Arrays are rejected (`INVALID_VALUE`), because `[lat, lng]` and GeoJSON's `[lng, lat]` are ambiguous.
- A `maps.app.goo.gl` short link cannot be expanded in the browser: open it and copy the full URL.

## `getMarkerPosition()` warns or returns 20,0

While the picker is unset, `getMarkerPosition()` returns the view centre (the 20,0 world view by default), not a chosen location, and warns once. Read `value` (`""` while unset) or `valueAsLatLng` (`null` while unset).

## React: handlers or properties are ignored

- `onError`, `onAddressChange` and `onReady` never fire on the element. Use the lowercase `onerror`, `onaddresschange` and `onready`; `location-picker/jsx/react` flags the wrong spelling as a type error.
- After `hydrateRoot` (Next.js App Router, Remix), React applies neither object props (`messages`, `geocoder`, …) nor lowercase native handlers. Set them in a ref callback: see the [React hydration recipe](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/frameworks.md#react-19-and-nextjs).
- React 18 sets attributes rather than properties, so binding `value` needs React 19.

## Google Maps

- **The picker shows OpenStreetMap although Google is loaded.** Google is never chosen implicitly. Add `provider="google"` (or `api-key`). The console hint `google.maps is loaded but no provider was chosen` says the same.
- **`API_KEY_MISSING`.** Add `api-key="YOUR_KEY"`, or load the Google Maps JS API before the picker.
- **`GOOGLE_AUTH_FAILED`.** Check the key's HTTP-referrer restrictions, billing, and that the Maps JavaScript API is enabled.
- **`MAP_ID_REQUIRED`.** `marker="advanced"` needs `map-id`; the CSS pin is used until then.
- **Search does nothing** (`GEOCODER_FAILED`). Enable Places API (New) for the key. On old pages that load Google with a classic script tag and no `importLibrary`, add `libraries=places`.
- **A pinch zoom changed the value.** On Google Maps a pinch zooms around the fingers, so the centre moves and the new centre is committed. Wheel, double-click and the zoom buttons stay anchored at the pin.

## The wheel scrolls the page instead of zooming

With the default `gesture-handling="auto"`, a page that scrolls gets cooperative gestures, so the map does not trap the scroll inside a form. Hold Ctrl (⌘ on Apple platforms) while scrolling, use the zoom buttons, or set `gesture-handling="greedy"`.

## Geolocation

- **The locate button is missing.** It is hidden when the page is not a secure context (use HTTPS or localhost) or the browser has no geolocation. In an iframe, the frame needs `allow="geolocation"`.
- **`GEOLOCATION_DENIED`, `GEOLOCATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `GEOLOCATION_TIMEOUT`.** `locate()` rejects with these codes. It never hangs: it uses a 10 s `timeout` plus a watchdog 30 s later, which also covers an unanswered permission prompt. Adjust with the `geolocation` property (`{ timeout: 5000 }`).
- **Nothing prompted on load.** That is the default. Use `locate="button"` (prompts on click) or `locate="auto"` (also tries once on load while unset).

## Search returns nothing

- Queries need at least 3 characters. Coordinates (`48.85, 2.29`, a map URL) jump directly without a request.
- The public Photon endpoint is fair-use and throttles heavy use. For production, self-host Photon or use a commercial endpoint ([providers.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/providers.md#photon)).
- Check your CSP `connect-src` for `https://photon.komoot.io`.
- `GEOCODER_MISMATCH` means the geocoder is not allowed with this map provider (for example Photon results on a Google map). Use the provider's own geocoder or a custom one with a matching `pairsWith`.

## Two copies of the library on one page

The ESM build, the CommonJS build and the script build share one global store, so Leaflet and Google are loaded once and the element is defined once (a warning appears if the versions differ). `instanceof LocationPickerElement` can still be false across copies; check with `customElements.get('location-picker')` or duck typing.

## Component tests in jsdom or happy-dom

These environments lack form internals, `ResizeObserver` and constructable stylesheets. The element then runs inert: it logs one message naming the missing API, never throws, and `value`, `valueAsLatLng` and `setLocation()` still round-trip. Test maps and forms in a real browser.

## Still stuck?

Open an issue with the `code` and `fix` from the console, how you load the library (script tag, npm entry), the provider, and a minimal page that reproduces it: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/issues

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/ai-agents.md

# AI agents

location-picker is written to be used correctly by coding agents as well as people: predictable names, loud errors with fixes, and documentation in the formats agents read.

## For agents writing code that uses location-picker

| Resource                                                                     | What it is                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [llms.txt](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/llms.txt)           | A short overview with the key rules, one runnable example and links ([llms.txt format](https://llmstxt.org/))                                                |
| [llms-full.txt](https://cyphercodes.github.io/location-picker/llms-full.txt) | The README and every page of `docs/` in one file                                                                                                             |
| `skills/location-picker/SKILL.md`                                            | An [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/), shipped in the npm package (`node_modules/location-picker/skills/location-picker/SKILL.md`) and in the repository |
| `custom-elements.json`                                                       | Custom Elements Manifest for the element (the package's `customElements` field): attributes, properties, events, parts, slots, states and CSS properties     |
| The `.d.ts` files                                                            | JSDoc with `@default` and `@example` on every option; the [API reference](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/api.md) quotes the same text                                                       |
| `context7.json`                                                              | Indexing configuration for [Context7](https://context7.com/)                                                                                                 |

To add the skill to a project with the skills CLI: `npx skills add cyphercodes/location-picker`.

### Rules that prevent most mistakes

1. Load `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3`, never the unpinned `/dist/location-picker.min.js` (that is the frozen v1 file).
2. `import 'location-picker'` defines `<location-picker>`; `location-picker/core` is the class only.
3. Latitude first: `"lat,lng"` strings or `{ lat, lng }` objects, never arrays.
4. In forms, use `name` (or `lat-name`/`lng-name`), or `lat-input`/`lng-input` for existing inputs. Put `required` on the picker.
5. Bind `value` in frameworks and listen to `change`/`input`. Never bind `lat`/`lng`.
6. Read the result from `value`/`valueAsLatLng` or the `change` event's `detail`, not `getMarkerPosition()`.
7. OpenStreetMap needs no key. Choose Google explicitly (`provider="google"` + `api-key`).
8. In React, the lowercase `onaddresschange`/`onready`/`onerror`; after `hydrateRoot`, set objects and listeners in a ref.

The full list with explanations is the "Common mistakes" section of the [README](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/README.md#common-mistakes).

### Debugging from the console

Every failure carries a stable `code` and a `fix`, in the form `[location-picker] <what happened>. Fix: <fix>`. Misspelled attributes (`latitude=`, `api_key=`, `lon=`, …) and unknown options log a warning that names the right one. The codes are listed in [errors.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/errors.md).

## WebMCP tools (experimental)

[WebMCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp/imperative-api) lets a page expose tools to an AI agent running in the browser. location-picker can register tools that read and set its location, so an agent does not have to drag a map. It is off by default, feature-detected, and does nothing where WebMCP is unavailable. The WebMCP API itself is still experimental and may change.

Turn it on with the `webmcp` attribute:

```html
<form method="post" action="/deliveries">
  <label for="drop">Drop-off point</label>
  <location-picker id="drop" name="dropoff" search webmcp style="height: 360px"></location-picker>
  <button>Continue</button>
</form>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/location-picker@3"></script>
```

Or call `registerWebMcpTools()` to describe what the location is for:

```ts
import 'location-picker';
import { isWebMcpSupported, registerWebMcpTools } from 'location-picker/webmcp';

const picker = document.querySelector('location-picker');
if (picker && isWebMcpSupported()) {
  const registration = registerWebMcpTools(picker, {
    purpose: 'Delivery drop-off point for this order.',
  });
  console.log(registration.tools); // e.g. ['location_picker_get_location', 'location_picker_set_location', …]
}
```

| Tool                     | Input                        | Result                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<prefix>_get_location`  | none (read-only)             | `{ value, lat, lng, address }`, or `{ value: "" }` while unset                              |
| `<prefix>_set_location`  | `{ lat, lng }` or `{ text }` | commits like `setLocation()` (source `api`); `text` is parsed as coordinates, else geocoded |
| `<prefix>_search_places` | `{ query }` (read-only)      | up to 5 results, not committed; registered only when a geocoder is available                |

- The prefix is `location_picker`, plus `_<id or name>` when the page has several pickers. Override it with `prefix`.
- There is never a locate tool: agents must not trigger permission prompts.
- An out-of-range latitude in `set_location` is a tool error, and nothing is committed.
- `unregister()` or aborting `signal` removes the tools.

## For agents working on this repository

Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/AGENTS.md): commands, layout, file ownership, test conventions and the rules for generated and frozen files.

---

Source: https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/api.md

# API reference

Every public export of `location-picker`, entry point by entry point. The descriptions quote the JSDoc that ships
in the package's `.d.ts` files, so your editor shows the same text on hover.

**Conventions**

- Latitude first, always. A value string is the canonical `"lat,lng"`: dot decimal, no spaces, `precision`
  decimals, trailing zeros trimmed, never `-0` (for example `"48.85837,2.294481"`).
- One name per concept: class option `fooBar` = element property `fooBar` = attribute `foo-bar` (the hyphen-less
  `foobar` is accepted too). Event `x` = class callback `onX`. The one exception is the locate control: option and
  attribute `locate`, readable property `locateMode`, because `locate()` is the method.
- Property writes are silent, like a native `<input>`. User gestures and method calls emit `input` (final value),
  then `change`, with `detail.source`.

**Entry points**

| Import                                                | Side effect                      | Section                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `location-picker`                                     | defines `<location-picker>`      | [root](#location-picker)                            |
| `location-picker/element`                             | defines `<location-picker>`      | [element](#location-pickerelement)                  |
| `location-picker/core`                                | none                             | [core](#location-pickercore)                        |
| `location-picker/utils`                               | none (DOM-free)                  | [utils](#location-pickerutils)                      |
| `location-picker/leaflet`                             | none                             | [leaflet](#location-pickerleaflet)                  |
| `location-picker/google`                              | none                             | [google](#location-pickergoogle)                    |
| `location-picker/maplibre`                            | none                             | [maplibre](#location-pickermaplibre)                |
| `location-picker/photon`                              | none                             | [photon](#location-pickerphoton)                    |
| `location-picker/webmcp`                              | none                             | [webmcp](#location-pickerwebmcp)                    |
| `location-picker/global`                              | runs the IIFE (`<script>` build) | [global](#location-pickerglobal)                    |
| `location-picker/style.css`                           | CSS                              | [style.css](#location-pickerstylecss)               |
| `location-picker/v1`                                  | v1 CSS injection                 | [v1](#location-pickerv1)                            |
| `location-picker/dist/location-picker.min.js`         | v1 CSS injection                 | [v1 file](#location-pickerdistlocation-pickerminjs) |
| `location-picker/jsx/{react,preact,solid,vue,svelte}` | none (types only)                | [jsx](#location-pickerjsxreact)                     |

Error codes and their fixes: [errors.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/errors.md). Behaviour in forms: [forms.md](https://github.com/cyphercodes/location-picker/blob/master/docs/forms.md).

## `location-picker`

The root entry. `import 'location-picker'`, `import { LocationPicker } from 'location-picker'` and the jsDelivr
`+esm` build all define `<location-picker>` as a side effect (no-op on the server). For a side-effect-free,
class-only import use `location-picker/core`.
CJS: `require('location-picker')` returns `{ LocationPicker, default: LocationPicker, LocationPickerElement, ... }`
(the v2 shape). The v1 shape `new (require(...))()` lives at `require('location-picker/v1')`.

- `export * from 'location-picker/core'`
- `export * from 'location-picker/element'`
- `export { default } from 'location-picker/core'`

## `location-picker/element`

- `export type { ChangeSource }`

### `LocationPickerElementEventMap`

Type: `type LocationPickerElementEventMap = Omit<HTMLElementEventMap, 'input' | 'change' | 'error'> & { input: CustomEvent<LocationDetail>; change: CustomEvent<LocationDetail>; addresschange: CustomEvent<AddressDetail>; ready: CustomEvent<ReadyDetail<unknown>>; error: CustomEvent<LocationPickerError>; }`

Element event map: native HTMLElement events with `input`/`change`/`error` replaced by the picker's CustomEvents.

### `LocationPickerElement`
